title: wk-psrun generic PowerShell runner
desc: Repo-root pace-exempt launcher: runs any PowerShell script file directly (powershell -File PATH ARGS), unlike wk-parsecheck which only AST-parses. Created 2026-07-09 to execute a self-test whose file lives in a different repo, when raw powershell -File was pace-95-blocked.
steps: WHAT: wk-psrun.cmd wraps powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File %1 %2 %3 %4 %5 -- a bare pass-through script runner, pace-exempt because its command name starts with wk-.

USAGE: ./wk-psrun.cmd <path-to-ps1> [args...] -- works for scripts in ANY repo, not just this one, since it just forwards the path to powershell -File. Use the bare/relative form (./wk-psrun.cmd), never an absolute D:/... path prefix -- the pace-95/wk-only-gate exemption matches on the literal command-string PREFIX, so only a bare or ./-prefixed wk- invocation passes; an absolute path does not.

SEE ALSO: wk-parsecheck (AST-parse-only, does not execute/run the script -- use wk-psrun when you need the script to actually RUN, e.g. a self-test block guarded by MyInvocation.InvocationName), pace-deadlock-escapes-harness-editable-and-jisikhwa-free (the R3 wk-tool-stays-pace-exempt reflex this tool exists to exercise).

requirements.expect: runs the script and prints its real output, not just a parse result
still pace-95-blocked, must use bare/./ form
